(abdominal part of pectoralis major musc: The lowest fibres, arising from the aponeurosis of external oblique; they form the anterior fold of the axilla.
(adductor minimus): The separate uppermost fibres of adductor magnus.
(iliopectineal bursa): Large bursa between the iliopsoas tendon and the hip capsule; it may communicate with the hip joint.
(opponens digiti minimi muscle of foot): Inconstant fibres of flexor digiti minimi brevis extending to the 5th metatarsal.
abductor digiti minimi of foot: Muscle on the lateral border of the sole; lateral plantar nerve.
abductor digiti minimi of hand: Superficial muscle of the hypothenar eminence; abducts the little finger. Ulnar nerve.
abductor hallucis: Muscle on the medial border of the sole; abducts the big toe and supports the medial arch. Medial plantar nerve.
abductor pollicis brevis: Superficial muscle of the thenar eminence; moves the thumb away from the palm at a right angle. Median nerve (recurrent branch); it wastes in carpal tunnel syndrome.
abductor pollicis longus: Inserts into the base of the 1st metacarpal; abducts the thumb. Its tendon runs in the 1st extensor compartment (De Quervain's tenosynovitis).
acetabular fossa: Non-articular floor of the acetabulum; contains fat and the ligament of the head of the femur.
acetabular labrum: Fibrocartilaginous ring around the rim of the acetabulum; it deepens the socket and holds the femoral head by suction. A tear causes groin pain.
acetabular margin: Rim of the acetabulum; the acetabular labrum attaches here and deepens the socket.
acetabular notch: Notch in the lower rim of the acetabulum; bridged by the transverse acetabular ligament, vessels pass through it.
acetabulum: Socket of the hip bone; formed by the union of ilium, ischium and pubis, it receives the femoral head.
acromial angle: Posterolateral corner of the acromion; a reference point for measuring arm length.
acromial end: Flattened lateral end of the clavicle; forms the acromioclavicular joint with the acromion.
acromial facet: Small articular facet at the lateral end; articulates with the acromion.
acromial part of deltoid muscle: Middle, multipennate fibres; abduct the arm from 15° up to 90°.
acromioclavicular ligament: Superior capsular thickening of the acromioclavicular joint; the first ligament to tear in the grading of shoulder separations.
acromion: Lateral end of the spine of the scapula; the highest point of the shoulder, it articulates with the clavicle.
adductor brevis: Muscle lying behind adductor longus; the anterior and posterior branches of the obturator nerve run in front of and behind it.
adductor longus: Runs from the body of the pubis to the linea aspera; forms the medial border of the femoral triangle. It is the muscle most often injured in groin strains.
adductor magnus: The largest adductor; its adductor part is supplied by the obturator nerve, its hamstring part by the tibial nerve. Through the adductor hiatus in its tendon the femoral vessels pass to the popliteal fossa.
adductor pollicis: Deep hand muscle with oblique and transverse heads; brings the thumb towards the palm. Ulnar nerve (deep branch).
adductor tubercle: Small prominence above the medial epicondyle; the hamstring part of adductor magnus attaches to it.
ala of ilium: Broad wing of the ilium; the iliac fossa lies on its inner surface and the gluteal muscles on its outer surface.
ala of sacrum: Lateral wing of the sacrum; the lumbosacral trunk passes in front of it.
anatomical neck of humerus: Constriction just below the articular cartilage of the humeral head; the capsule attaches here.
anconeus muscle: Small triangular muscle from the lateral epicondyle to the olecranon; assists elbow extension. Radial nerve.
angle of rib: Point where the rib curves forwards at the back; the commonest site of rib fractures.
annular epiphysis: Bony ring around the upper and lower surfaces of a vertebral body.
annular ligament of radius: Ring holding the radial head against the radial notch of the ulna; in pulled elbow in young children the head slips out of this ring.
anserine bursa: Beneath the sartorius, gracilis and semitendinosus tendons; its inflammation causes pain on the lower medial side of the knee.
antebrachial fascia: Deep fascia enclosing the forearm; it thickens towards the wrist to form the retinacula.
anterior arch of atlas: Short anterior arch of the atlas; on its inner surface is a facet that articulates with the dens.
anterior articular facet of dens axis: Front surface of the dens; articulates with the anterior arch of the atlas.
anterior belly of digastric muscle: Runs from the digastric fossa of the mandible to the intermediate tendon; supplied by the nerve to mylohyoid (V3), it opens the mouth.
anterior border of fibula: Anterior border of the fibula; the septum separating the anterior and lateral compartments attaches to it.
anterior border of tibia: Sharp anterior border felt under the skin (the shin).
anterior cells of ethmoid bone: Anterior air cells of the ethmoidal labyrinth; they open into the middle meatus.
anterior clinoid process: Backward-projecting tip of the lesser wing; the tentorium cerebelli attaches to it and it lies beside the internal carotid artery.
anterior cruciate ligament: Runs from the anterior intercondylar area of the tibia to the inner surface of the lateral femoral condyle; prevents forward sliding of the tibia. Often torn in sports injuries (anterior drawer, Lachman test).
anterior gluteal line: Anterior line on the outer surface of the ilium; separates the origins of gluteus medius and minimus.
anterior inferior iliac spine: Projection below the ASIS; the straight head of rectus femoris and the iliofemoral ligament attach to it.
anterior intercondylar area: Anterior area between the condyles; the anterior cruciate ligament and the anterior horns of the menisci attach to it.
anterior intermuscular septum of leg: Fascial wall separating the anterior and lateral compartments.
anterior layer of thoracolumbar fascia: Layer covering the front of quadratus lumborum.
anterior ligament of fibular head: Ligament reinforcing the superior tibiofibular joint in front.
